fullPassage:
Logan's Speech

"The assignment is to write a speech about someone who you admire. It could be a historical figure, a celebrity, or even someone you personally know in your life," Ms. Harper told the class. My classmates began brainstorming a list of people they might pick — mostly athletes, singers, and actors. However, I knew right away who my speech was going to be about. Grandma is the person I admire the most. Writing a speech about her would be a piece of cake.

A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to deliver a good speech. This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of standing in front of the entire class made my palms sweat. I'm too shy to raise my hand in class even when I know the answer. How on earth can I speak in front of everyone? I couldn't sleep at all that night.

The big day for the speech finally arrived, and I felt more anxious than ever. I had spent the previous week imagining how my classmates would react to my speech. I was still mostly thinking about what my classmates might think. I wasn't putting much thought into what I was actually going to say. I figured I could just speak off the top of my head. After all, I was going to talk about my grandmother. I didn't need any notes.

I was sweating as I walked up to the front of the class. My heart was racing so fast that I thought it might fly out of my chest. I could feel my face turning red. I didn't know where to look. I blanked out. I just stood there silently.

Ms. Harper tried to help me out. "Start by telling us a bit about your grandmother, Logan." I spoke about what kind of work my grandmother used to do, but I quickly ran out of words to say. Then Ms. Harper said, "How about telling us a bit about why you admire her so much?" I barely managed to share a short story about her. After that, I just rushed to my seat and put my head in my hands. I knew I had messed up. I hadn't said all the things I wanted to say.

The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to talk about the speech. I said, "I'm embarrassed about the speech. I must have looked like a fool. I know I could have done better."

"It's quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it," she said in a warm voice. "What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?"

"I was afraid the other students would laugh at me if my speech wasn't good enough."

She replied, "You certainly can't control what others think about your speech. That means you should be focusing on the one thing you can control — how you give your speech." That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! I wouldn't have been able to make my classmates like what I wanted to say. I really should have focused on my performance.

A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts. I rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause.

I felt nervous again when the big day finally arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I noticed that my nerves had actually calmed down a bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I walked up to the front of the class and looked out into the audience. My heart began to race, and I took a deep breath to calm it down. While my voice trembled from time to time, I managed to get my whole message across. When I was done, I felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was clapping for me!

The Golden Rule of Listening

Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your listener?

Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.

Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.

questions.passage: "The assignment is to write a speech about someone who you (A)[admire / acquire]. It could be a historical figure, a celebrity, or even someone you personally know in your life," Ms. Harper told the class. My classmates began (B)[brainstorming / broadcasting] a list of people they might pick — mostly athletes, singers, and actors. However, I knew right away who my speech was going to be about. Writing a speech about her would be a piece of (C)[cake / work].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 존경하는 사람에 대해 발표문을 쓰는 과제. 반 친구들은 목록을 만들어 내기 위해 아이디어를 끌어내기 시작했다. 할머니에 대한 발표문 쓰기는 식은 죽 먹기.
det.analysis:
✅ ① admire — brainstorming — cake
❌ ② acquire — brainstorming — work
❌ ③ admire — broadcasting — work
❌ ④ acquire — broadcasting — cake
✅ (A) admire: '존경하다'가 문맥에 적합. acquire(획득하다)는 맥락 불일치. ✅ (B) brainstorming: '아이디어를 끌어내다'. broadcasting(방송하다)은 목록 작성과 무관. ✅ (C) cake: 'a piece of cake'는 '식은 죽 먹기' 관용구. 'a piece of work'는 다른 의미.
det.tip: a piece of cake = 아주 쉬운 일. brainstorm = 아이디어를 짜내다/브레인스토밍하다.

questions.passage: I was still mostly thinking about what my classmates might think. I wasn't putting much (A)[thought / effort] into what I was actually going to say. I figured I could just speak off the top of my (B)[head / mind]. After all, I was going to talk about my grandmother. I didn't need any (C)[notes / advice].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 반 친구들이 어떻게 생각할지에 대해 생각하고 있었다. 실제로 무슨 말을 할지에 대해서는 깊이 생각하지 않았다. 머릿속에서 떠오르는 대로 말할 수 있을 것이라 생각했다. 원고가 필요 없었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① effort — head — advice
❌ ② effort — mind — notes
✅ ③ thought — head — notes
❌ ④ thought — mind — advice
✅ (A) thought: 'put thought into'는 '~에 대해 생각을 기울이다'. effort(노력)도 가능하지만 원문은 thought. ✅ (B) head: 'off the top of my head'는 '즉흥적으로' 관용 표현. mind는 쓰지 않는 표현. ✅ (C) notes: '원고/메모'가 맥락에 적합. advice(조언)는 무관.
det.tip: off the top of one's head = 즉흥적으로, 생각나는 대로. put thought into = ~에 대해 깊이 생각하다.

questions.passage: "It's quite all right to fall (A)[short / behind] of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it," she said in a warm voice. She replied, "You certainly can't control what others think about your speech. That means you should be focusing on the one thing you can control — how you give your speech." That woke me up from the (B)[depths / limits] of despair. I really should have focused on my (C)[performance / appearance].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 자신의 기대에 미치지 못한 것은 배울 수 있는 한 괜찮다. 그 말씀이 절망의 늪에서 나를 깨웠다. 나는 사실 내 발표에 집중했어야 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① short — depths — performance
❌ ② behind — depths — appearance
❌ ③ short — limits — appearance
❌ ④ behind — limits — performance
✅ (A) short: 'fall short of'는 '~에 미치지 못하다'. fall behind(뒤처지다)는 of와 결합 불가. ✅ (B) depths: 'depths of despair'는 '절망의 깊은 곳'. limits(한계)는 despair와 결합 부자연. ✅ (C) performance: '발표(수행)'에 집중. appearance(외모)는 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: fall short of = ~에 미치지 못하다. the depths of despair = 절망의 나락. performance = 수행, 공연, 발표.

questions.passage: A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to deliver a good speech. This ①<u>reminded</u> me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of standing in front of the entire class made my palms ②<u>sweat</u>. I'm too ③<u>shy</u> to raise my hand in class even when I know the answer. I couldn't sleep at all that night because I was so ④<u>relieved</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 발표를 해야 한다는 사실이 상기되었고, 손에 땀이 났고, 수줍음이 많아 손도 못 들었다. 그날 밤 잠을 못 잤다. 안심한 것이 아니라 불안했기 때문.
det.analysis: ✅ ①reminded(상기시켰다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②sweat(땀이 나다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③shy(수줍은): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④relieved(안심한): 원문 맥락은 불안/긴장. 잠을 못 잔 이유가 '안심'이면 모순.
det.tip: relieved(안심한) ↔ anxious/nervous(불안한). 잠을 못 잔 맥락은 불안이므로 relieved는 부적절.

questions.passage: I was sweating as I walked up to the front of the class. My heart was ①<u>racing</u> so fast that I thought it might fly out of my chest. I could feel my face turning red. I ②<u>calmed</u> out. I just stood there ③<u>silently</u>. Ms. Harper tried to help me out. I spoke about what kind of work my grandmother used to do, but I quickly ran out of words to say. I knew I had ④<u>messed</u> up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 심장이 빨리 뛰고, 얼굴이 빨개지고, 머릿속이 텅 비었다. '진정했다(calmed)'가 아니라 '텅 비었다(blanked)'가 맞다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①racing(빨리 뛰는): 원문 그대로. ❌ ②calmed(진정했다): 원문은 blanked(머릿속이 텅 비다). 극도로 긴장한 상황에서 '진정했다'는 맥락 모순. ✅ ③silently(조용히): 원문 그대로. ✅ ④messed(망쳤다): 원문 그대로.
det.tip: blanked out(머릿속이 텅 비다) ↔ calmed out(진정하다). 긴장 상태에서 blanked가 자연스러움.

questions.passage: A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to ①<u>drop the ball</u> like the first time. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I used cue cards which contained key phrases about ②<u>important</u> facts. I ③<u>rehearsed</u> how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause. While my voice trembled from time to time, I managed to get my whole message ④<u>lost</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 실수로 망치고 싶지 않았다. 메모 카드를 활용하고 예행연습을 했다. 내용을 모두 전달했다. 잃어버린 것이 아니라 전달(across)한 것.
det.analysis: ✅ ①drop the ball(실수로 망치다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②important(중요한): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③rehearsed(예행연습했다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④lost(잃어버린): 원문은 'across'(get ~ across = 전달하다). 메시지를 잃은 것이 아니라 전달한 것.
det.tip: get one's message across = 메시지를 전달하다. drop the ball = 실수하다/기회를 놓치다.

questions.passage: A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to deliver a good speech. This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of standing in front of the entire class made my palms sweat. I'm too shy to raise my hand in class even when I know the answer. How on earth can I speak in front of everyone? I couldn't sleep at all that night.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Logan felt extremely __________ about giving a speech in front of the class.

det.korean: 반 전체 앞에 선다는 생각에 손에 땀이 나고, 답을 알 때도 손을 들지 못할 정도로 수줍음이 많았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②nervous(긴장한): 손에 땀이 나고 수줍음을 타는 것은 긴장의 표현. ❌ ①confident(자신감 있는): 반대 상황. ❌ ③excited(신나는): 긴장이지 흥분이 아님. ❌ ④bored(지루한): 무관.
det.tip: nervous = 긴장한, 불안한. palms sweat(손에 땀이 나다)은 긴장의 신체 반응.

questions.passage: Ms. Harper tried to help me out. "Start by telling us a bit about your grandmother, Logan." I spoke about what kind of work my grandmother used to do, but I quickly ran out of words to say. I barely managed to share a short story about her. After that, I just rushed to my seat and put my head in my hands. I knew I had messed up. I hadn't said all the things I wanted to say.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

After the failed speech, Logan felt a deep sense of __________.

det.korean: 자리로 돌아와 두 손으로 머리를 감쌌다. 망쳤다는 걸 알았고, 말하고 싶었던 것을 다 말하지 못했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③regret(후회): 망친 후 말하지 못한 것에 대한 아쉬움/후회. ❌ ①pride(자부심): 반대. ❌ ②relief(안도): 반대. ❌ ④curiosity(호기심): 무관.
det.tip: regret = 후회, 아쉬움. 'messed up' + 'hadn't said all the things'는 후회의 맥락.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The passage suggests that good listeners contribute to a __________ atmosphere during speeches.

det.korean: 좋은 청자는 긍정적인 의사소통 분위기를 만들어 발표자를 돕는다. 관심을 갖고 주의 깊게 들어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④supportive(도움이 되는): positive communication climate과 동의. ❌ ①competitive(경쟁적인): 청취와 무관. ❌ ②critical(비판적인): 긍정적 분위기와 반대. ❌ ③tense(긴장된): 반대.
det.tip: supportive = 도움이 되는, 지지하는. positive communication climate = 긍정적 소통 분위기.

questions.passage: "The assignment is to write a speech about someone who you <u>admire</u>."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 admire와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 존경하는 사람에 대해 발표문을 쓰는 과제.
det.analysis: ✅ ②respect(존경하다): admire의 동의어. ❌ ①ignore(무시하다): 반의어. ❌ ③envy(부러워하다): 존경과 시기는 다름. ❌ ④dislike(싫어하다): 반의어.
det.tip: admire = respect = look up to = 존경하다.

questions.passage: I <u>barely</u> managed to share a short story about her. After that, I just rushed to my seat.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 barely와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 할머니에 대한 짧은 이야기를 간신히 전했다. 그러고 나서 자리로 황급히 돌아왔다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①hardly(간신히, 거의 ~않게): barely의 동의어. ❌ ②easily(쉽게): 반대. ❌ ③quickly(빠르게): barely는 빈도/정도의 문제. ❌ ④frequently(자주): 무관.
det.tip: barely = hardly = scarcely = 간신히, 겨우. 부정의 뉘앙스를 가진 부사.

questions.passage: I <u>rehearsed</u> how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 rehearsed와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 어떻게 서 있을지, 어떻게 청중과 눈을 맞출지, 언제 멈출지 예행연습했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③practiced(연습하다): rehearse의 동의어. ❌ ①imagined(상상하다): 상상만 한 것이 아님. ❌ ②avoided(피하다): 반대. ❌ ④abandoned(포기하다): 반대.
det.tip: rehearse = practice = 연습하다/예행연습하다. 주로 공연, 발표 등의 사전 연습에 사용.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 anxious의 반의어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그 어느 때보다 더 불안했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④calm(차분한): anxious의 반의어. ❌ ①worried(걱정하는): anxious의 유의어. ❌ ②fearful(두려운): 유의어. ❌ ③nervous(긴장한): 유의어.
det.tip: anxious(불안한) ↔ calm(차분한). 유의어: worried, nervous, fearful, uneasy.

questions.passage: When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be <u>constructive</u> and helpful.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 constructive의 반의어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람의 발표를 논의하거나 비평할 때는 건설적이고 도움이 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②destructive(파괴적인): constructive의 반의어. ❌ ①positive(긍정적인): constructive의 유의어. ❌ ③productive(생산적인): 유의어. ❌ ④creative(창의적인): 다른 개념.
det.tip: constructive(건설적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). con-(함께 세우다) vs de-(허물다).

questions.passage: A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to <u>deliver</u> a good speech. This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of standing in front of the entire class made my palms sweat.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 deliver의 이 글에서의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Harper 선생님은 좋은 발표를 하는 방법에 대해 말했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③전달하다 (발표하다): deliver a speech = 발표하다. ❌ ①배달하다: 택배 등의 의미. ❌ ②출산하다: 의학적 의미. ❌ ④구출하다: 구어체에서 드물게 사용.
det.tip: deliver: (1)배달하다 (2)발표하다/연설하다 (3)출산하다 (4)구출하다. 'deliver a speech'에서는 '발표하다'.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to practice a play, speech, or piece of music in preparation for a public performance"

det.korean: "공개 공연을 위해 연극, 발표, 또는 음악을 연습하다"
det.analysis: ✅ ③rehearse: 공연/발표를 위한 예행연습. ❌ ①memorize(암기하다): 연습과 다름. ❌ ②improvise(즉흥으로 하다): 반대 개념. ❌ ④compose(작곡하다/작성하다): 무관.
det.tip: rehearse = 예행연습하다. 본문 'I rehearsed how I would stand'에서 등장.

questions.passage: I felt more anxious than ever. I had spent the previous week imagining how my classmates would react to my speech. I was still mostly thinking about what my classmates might think.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

Her __________ (anxious) about the presentation kept her awake all night.

det.korean: 발표에 대한 그녀의 불안감이 밤새 잠을 못 자게 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ anxiety: 소유격 Her 뒤이므로 명사 형태. anxious(형용사) → anxiety(명사).
det.tip: anxious(형용사: 불안한) → anxiety(명사: 불안감). 'Her + 명사' 구조.

questions.passage: "I'm embarrassed about the speech. I must have looked like a fool. I know I could have done better."
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

The __________ (embarrass) moment on stage made him want to disappear.

det.korean: 무대 위의 당혹스러운 순간이 그를 사라지고 싶게 만들었다.
det.analysis: ✅ embarrassing: 관사 The와 명사 moment 사이이므로 형용사. '사람이 아닌 상황/순간'이 주어이므로 -ing형(감정 유발). embarrassed는 '사람이 느끼는 감정'.
det.tip: embarrassed(당혹감을 느끼는 — 사람) vs embarrassing(당혹감을 유발하는 — 상황/사물). moment는 사물이므로 embarrassing.

questions.passage: A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used __________ which contained key phrases about important facts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이번에는 매일 거울 앞에 서서 연습했고, 중요한 사실에 대한 핵심 표현들을 담은 것을 활용했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②cue cards: 원문 그대로. 핵심 표현이 담긴 메모 카드. ❌ ①textbooks(교과서): 발표 연습에 교과서는 부적절. ❌ ③cell phones(휴대전화): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④notebooks(공책): key phrases를 담은 것은 카드.
det.tip: cue card = 메모 카드. 발표 시 핵심 내용을 적어두는 작은 카드.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you
Always give feedback after someone finishes speaking
Take notes on everything the speaker says
Focus on finding mistakes in the speaker's argument

det.korean: 잘 듣는 것은 말을 잘하는 것만큼 중요하다. 누구나 더 나은 청자가 될 수 있다. 경청의 황금률을 기억하라.
det.analysis: ✅ ①Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you: 원문 그대로. 경청의 황금률. ❌ ②Always give feedback: 피드백은 경청의 핵심이 아님. ❌ ③Take notes: 메모는 언급되지 않음. ❌ ④Focus on finding mistakes: 비판적 태도는 constructive and helpful과 반대.
det.tip: Golden Rule of Listening = 경청의 황금률. '남에게 대접받고 싶은 대로 남을 대접하라'의 경청 버전.
